identity.title: General framework for online-to-nonconvex conversion: Schedule-free SGD is also effective for nonconvex optimization

problem.claim: Assess whether schedule-free methods, motivated by neural-network training results, are effective for nonconvex optimization.

gap.claim: Convex theory does not explain parameter choices for schedule-free SGD, leaving a theoretical gap.

contributions.claim: A general online-to-nonconvex conversion framework that turns an online learning algorithm into an optimization algorithm for nonconvex losses.
Two novel conversion schemes, including one that directly yields schedule-free SGD.
An analysis establishing schedule-free SGD’s optimal iteration complexity for nonsmooth, non-convex optimization.

stated_novelty.claim: The framework recovers existing conversions and introduces two new schemes; one directly corresponds to schedule-free SGD.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that schedule-free SGD achieves optimal iteration complexity for nonsmooth, non-convex optimization problems.
The authors report that their framework recovers existing conversions and produces two novel conversion schemes.
The authors report that their analysis provides insight into schedule-free SGD parameter choices beyond what convex theory explains.

narrative_sequence.summary: The work examines schedule-free methods in nonconvex optimization, motivated by their reported empirical success in neural-network training.
The proof develops a general conversion from online learning algorithms to nonconvex optimization algorithms.
The framework recovers prior conversions and yields two new schemes.
One new scheme is schedule-free SGD, enabling the authors’ claimed optimality result and parameter-choice insights.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links the algorithmic result to a general conversion framework and separately identifies the parameter-choice gap left by convex theory.

lessons.interpretation: This pairing makes the methodological mechanism and the specific explanatory payoff visible together.
lessons.application: When presenting a theory result, state both the reusable transformation that generates it and the concrete limitation in prior theory that the analysis addresses.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when a paper’s contribution is primarily empirical or lacks a generalizable mechanism.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the iteration-complexity rate, optimization assumptions, oracle model, or meaning of optimality.
The parameter recommendations and the two conversion schemes are not described in enough detail to assess their scope or applicability.
